how: Calls recruited helpers for lettering, a burger and a face, including requests to other subreddits.
A member offered an unfinished burger and received a promise to contribute.
Members answered building invitations with bare promises to contribute.
Starting and calling occur within one invitation rather than demonstrating two successive stages.
Bare acceptance is visible, but an obligation on every reader and a preference structure cannot be established from the observed pair.
A participant explained building difficulty by the community's small size.
Relocation was justified by blocked space, while the explicit small-community explanation followed the switch rather than demonstrating a prior judgment causing it.
The work moved among a face, a logo and additional lettering rather than retaining one settled design.
Participants reported work still underway and announced completed pictures.
Calls, acceptance and progress reports support an observed sequence without establishing which invitation caused unrecorded placements.
Images, exact coordinates and requests for templates made participation possible.
An image proposed at the outset does not establish prior design disagreement settled by an agreed template.
A member claimed three accounts and another suggested a script, without demonstrating collective automation.
Chat routing moved requests out of scattered threads and returned decisions to Reddit, without making the unseen deliberation observable.
The room requested dedicated defenders and reported a chat decision, so a local absence of decided order cannot be inferred from the cross-room frequency claim.
Participants described protection shifts, called for dedicated defence and recruited latecomers to upkeep.
A repair call after placement stopped shows continued repair talk rather than a possible intervention on the shared canvas.
A progress report led within its reply branch to a request for defenders while the face was still being built.
Extra accounts and proposed scripts do not show upkeep causing machine adoption, while reported enemy bots prompted a proposal for synchronized people.
Participants attributed losses and admitted damage, without independently verifying the placement histories behind their accounts.
Neighbours negotiated background overlap, permission, shared borders and compromises around existing drawings.
Participants offered to spare a drawing and retained another sign's border in their own design.
A stated border compromise explicitly connected keeping the neighbour's border with retaining the room's lettering.
Help was sought and offered conditionally in return for accommodating neighbours or moving.
Outside help was requested under strain, but the cited record does not establish that requested placers arrived.
Agreement that the face should move elicited a conditional pixel offer rather than demonstrating delivered reciprocal help.
Wanting allies and proposing exchanges do not establish coalition membership or mutual defence.
Protection and interest in allies do not show a coalition formed because of upkeep pressure.
Participants relocated the face attempt and switched the project to a smaller logo.
Neighbour negotiation occurred during contested construction, without requiring a completed upkeep phase first.
The project switch redirected members to a new build that was subsequently reported complete.
The relocated logo became a new object of protection after the original face was abandoned.
Reported permission from a host diplomat supports guest access without establishing continuing host enforcement.
A member relayed an outside proposal while explicitly denying official mediator status.
Denying mediator status and referring permission requests elsewhere show uncertain representation rather than demonstrated rejection of a binding agreement.
The record shows authority disclaimers and referrals but does not show a settled agreement provoking members to reject its binding force.
Familiar fandom references supplied the proposed mark and the language used to rally contributors.
Canvas-space refusals do not establish a quarrel inherited from before the event.
Fandom references name the proposed work without demonstrating a prior tie naming an attack target.
A recruiting call alone cannot establish whether the host's April Fools framing made such calls potentially deceptive.
Complaining about scattered threads and requesting chat does not establish host regulation of canvas posts.
Calls and thread friction do not establish the proposed flood-to-host-regulation mechanism.
Participants thanked contributors, credited a drawing and celebrated representation on the finished canvas.
Reporting completion and celebrating it can occur in one passage rather than successive phases.
Participants recorded loss, regretted damage and described the final fate of their designs.
A celebration drew a reply assessing damage without establishing that celebration caused a preservation project.
An imagined offline version preserved the hoped-for design before the event's outcome was known.
An advance offline fallback and final celebration do not establish a later purpose or continuation of the temporary effort.
Recording loss and celebrating representation do not demonstrate a subsequent decision about carrying the effort forward.
Regret, apology and an explanation of damage do not resolve whether members contested which shared version should be preserved.
Participants carried the contest beyond closure by blaming attackers and describing divided loyalties.
Admitted greed and contested overlap support encroachment only without establishing an organized attack call by the room.
A call to make the face and later compromise requests do not establish that recruiting caused a turn to attacking.
Sparing proposals and apologies do not establish an attack-call and reasoned-refusal pair.
Compromise is explicit, but its initiation by the room's attack call remains unobserved.
Reported destruction and later blame show an experienced contest without proving that an attack call from the room caused it.
